title: Low Row Machine
summary: A plate-loaded seated row that pulls from low to your waist, mostly for the lats and mid-back.

equipment_needs.text: Needs: commercial gym machine (this exercise's own machine); weight plates.

muscles.why: Library rating 1 for upper back (main mover): each working set adds 1 of a set to the weekly upper back total.
Library rating 0.8 for lats (main mover): each working set adds 0.8 of a set to the weekly lats total.
Library rating 0.6 for traps (helper): each working set adds 0.6 of a set to the weekly traps total.
Library rating 0.5 for biceps (helper): each working set adds 0.5 of a set to the weekly biceps total.
Library rating 0.4 for rear delts (helper): each working set adds 0.4 of a set to the weekly rear delts total.

setup.text: Sit with your chest against the pad and take the low handles.
Pull your elbows back past your torso.
Let your arms go forward fully so your shoulder blades spread.

form_cues.cue: Pull the handles toward your hips
Keep the chest on the pad
Keep your chest on the pad the whole time.

mistakes.text: Lifting off the chest pad to move the weight.

lower_risk.text: Warm-up: the app adds up to 2 ramp-up sets only when the load is heavy for the equipment and the main muscle is not warm yet.
The app suggests a heavier load only when the jump is 7.5% or less; otherwise it adds a rep first.
Default target: 8-12 reps, stopping about 3 reps short of failure (RIR 3). Stop the set when form breaks down.
Use the same controlled range on every rep; lower under control rather than dropping or bouncing.
Pick a variation and range you can train pain-free.

alternatives.why: Swap sheet: More stretch emphasis, Less upper-back focus.
Swap sheet: Steadier cable tension, Narrower grip, Neutral grip (palms facing in).

alternatives.goal_label: Home gym: no equipment / bar only
alternatives.why: Swap sheet: Less stable, Lower loading potential, More technical.
